questions.question:
What is the time complexity of a Binary Search algorithm in the worst case?
a. O(n)
b. O(log n)
c. O(n²)
d. O(1)
questions.explanation: Binary search halves the interval at each step, so the worst case needs about log₂ n comparisons: O(log n). That is possible only on a sorted array.

questions.question:
Binary Search can be categorized into which of the following?
a) Graph algorithm
b) Divide and conquer
c) Greedy algorithm
d) Dynamic programming
questions.explanation: Binary search discards one half of the sorted range each time and continues on the other, which is divide and conquer. It is not greedy, dynamic programming or a graph algorithm.

questions.question:
What is the time complexity of binary search with iteration?
a) O(n log n)
b) O(log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(n²)
questions.explanation: The iterative version keeps low and high indices and halves the range per pass, giving O(log n) time with O(1) extra space. Recursion would add stack space.

questions.question:
Time complexity of worst case for Linear Search is ________.
a) O(1)
b) O(log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(n²)
questions.explanation: Linear search may compare against every element when the target is last or absent, so the worst case is O(n). Its best case is O(1).

questions.question:
Which of the following has search efficiency of O(1)?
a) Tree
b) Heap
c) Hash Table
d) Linked-List
questions.explanation: A hash table computes the slot directly from the key, giving O(1) average search. Trees and heaps average O(log n) and linked lists O(n).

questions.question:
If several elements are competing for the same bucket in the hash table, what is it called?
a) Diffusion
b) Replication
c) Collision
d) Duplication
questions.explanation: When two different keys hash to the same slot they collide, and the table must resolve it by chaining or probing. Replication and diffusion are not the terms for it.

questions.question:
Which of the following hashing collision resolution techniques uses a linked list to resolve collisions?
a. Linear Probing
b. Quadratic Probing
c. Double Hashing
d. Chaining
questions.explanation: Chaining keeps a linked list of all keys that hash to a slot, so colliding entries are simply appended. Probing techniques instead search for another free slot.

questions.question:
What is a hash table?
a) A structure that maps values to keys
b) A structure that maps keys to values
c) A structure used for storage
d) A structure used to implement stack and queue

options.A: A structure that maps values to keys
options.B: A structure that maps keys to values
options.D: A structure used to implement stack and queue

questions.explanation: A hash table stores key-value pairs and uses a hash function to locate the slot for a key, so it maps keys to values, not values to keys.

questions.question:
The following numbers are inserted into an empty binary search tree in the given order: 10, 1, 3, 5, 15, 12, 16. What is the number of leaf nodes of the binary search tree?
a) 3
b) 4
c) 5
d) 6
questions.explanation: Inserting 10, 1, 3, 5, 15, 12, 16 gives leaves 5 (under 3), 12 and 16 (under 15), so there are three leaves. Nodes 10, 1, 3 and 15 all have children.

questions.question:
A binary tree is balanced if the difference of height between left and right sub-tree is not more than ________.
a) 0
b) 1
c) 2
d) 3
questions.explanation: A height-balanced tree allows the two subtree heights to differ by at most 1, so every balance factor is -1, 0 or +1. Larger differences trigger rotations.

questions.question:
What is another name of height balanced binary search tree?
a) Red-Black Tree
b) AVL Tree
c) B-Tree
d) Splay Tree
questions.explanation: AVL trees, named after Adelson-Velsky and Landis, were the first height-balanced binary search trees. Red-black trees are balanced too but carry a different name.

questions.question:
Balance factor of AVL tree is ________.
a) height(left subtree) - height(right subtree)
b) height(right subtree) - height(left subtree)
c) height(left subtree) + height(right subtree)
d) height(left subtree) × height(right subtree)
questions.explanation: Balance factor = height(left subtree) - height(right subtree), and an AVL tree keeps it within -1, 0 and +1. The reverse subtraction is an alternative convention.

questions.question:
The process where two rotations are required to balance a tree is called ________.
a) Single rotation
b) Double rotation
c) Triple rotation
d) AVL rotation
questions.explanation: When the imbalance lies in the inner subtree (left-right or right-left), one rotation is not enough and a double rotation restores balance. A single rotation handles the outer cases.

questions.question:
Given an array arr = {45, 77, 89, 90, 94, 99, 100} and key = 99; what are the mid values (corresponding array elements) in the first and second levels of recursion?
a) 90 and 99
b) 90 and 94
c) 89 and 99
d) 89 and 94
questions.explanation: With seven elements the first mid is index 3, value 90; since 99 > 90 the search moves right, where the next mid is index 5, value 99. The key is found there.

questions.question:
Worst case for linear search is ________.
a) O(1)
b) O(log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(n²)
questions.explanation: Linear search compares elements one after another, so an absent or last element costs n comparisons: O(n). Only a hit at the first position is O(1).

What is the worst-case time complexity of searching in a Binary Search Tree (BST)?
a) O(1)
b) O(log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(n log n)
questions.explanation: An unbalanced BST can degenerate into a chain of n nodes, so a search may visit every node: O(n). A balanced tree keeps it at O(log n).

questions.question:
Which of the following balanced BST guarantees O(log n) search, insert, and delete operations?
a) Unbalanced BST
b) AVL Tree
c) Linked List
d) Array
questions.explanation: AVL trees rebalance by rotation after every insert or delete, so the height stays O(log n) and all three operations cost O(log n).

questions.question:
In Linear Probing collision resolution, if a slot is occupied, the next slot is probed using which formula?
a) (h(k) + i²) mod m
b) (h(k) + i) mod m
c) (h1(k) + i × h2(k)) mod m
d) (h(k) × i) mod m
questions.explanation: Linear probing tries successive slots with (h(k) + i) mod m for i = 0, 1, 2, and so on, so it scans forward until a free slot appears. Quadratic probing squares i instead.

questions.question:
Symbol tables in compilers are most efficiently implemented using which data structure?
a) Array
b) Linked List
c) Hash Table
d) Stack
questions.explanation: Compilers keep variable and function names in a symbol table, and a hash table gives O(1) average lookup for that. Arrays and lists would need linear search.

Which collision resolution technique uses a second hash function to determine the probe step size?
a) Linear Probing
b) Quadratic Probing
c) Double Hashing
d) Chaining
questions.explanation: Double hashing uses a second hash function to set the step: (h1(k) + i·h2(k)) mod m. A good h2 spreads keys better and avoids the clustering of linear probing.
